age.evidence: Only adult (8-10 weeks of age) male mice were used

sex.evidence: Only adult (8-10 weeks of age) male mice were used to establish foundational experimental outcomes.

dosing.evidence: DOI and LPS, or vehicle control (sterile 0.9% saline), were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.) at 10 ml/kg ... mice were injected (i.p.) with varying doses of DOI (0.1, 0.3, 0.56, 1.0, or 2.0 mg/kg) or vehicle

assays.assay_description: Locomotor activity measured in 25 × 25 × 20 cm open-field Plexiglas chambers for 10 min using an automated 16-beam infrared detection system; total distance and proportion of center time were recorded.

application_type.evidence: DOI and LPS, or vehicle control (sterile 0.9% saline), were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were allowed to acclimate to the behavioral room for 1 h prior to testing ... Mice were then placed in individual locomotion chambers for 10 min (room acclimation only, no apparatus habituation).

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in individual locomotion chambers (25 × 25 × 20 cm open-field Plexiglas cages) for 10 min — freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard OFT chamber; no food in apparatus during the 10-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard OFT chamber; no water in apparatus during the 10-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: DOI ... was administered 24 h prior to LPS ... and behavioral testing was conducted 24 h later (i.e., ~48 h after DOI).

sample_size.evidence: Mice (n = 12) were pretreated (i.p.) with DOI (0.3 or 1 mg/kg) or saline 24 h prior to LPS (1 mg/kg, i.p.), and locomotor activity (A) and center time (B) in the OFT was tested (for 10 min) 24 h later.

outcomes.summary: LPS significantly reduced total locomotor activity compared to saline. DOI 0.3 mg/kg pretreatment prevented this deficit and restored locomotor activity to control levels, whereas 1 mg/kg did not. Center time was unaffected by either LPS or DOI.
outcomes.statistics: Total distance: F[3,44] = 5.46, p < 0.01; Center time: F[3,44] = 0.17, p > 0.05
outcomes.evidence: LPS significantly reduced total locomotor activity compared with saline controls ... Pretreatment with DOI at 0.3 mg/kg effectively prevented these deficits, restoring locomotor activity to control levels ... the 1 mg/kg treatment did not mitigate the LPS-induced behavioral deficit

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total distance is expressed as the sum of surround and center distances. Center time was calculated as the proportion of time spent moving in the center of the arena.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Outcomes reported as totals/proportions over the entire 10-min session.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or sequence analysis reported.

D5_followup.evidence: DOI was administered 24 h prior to LPS, and behavioral testing was conducted 24 h later — ~48 h after the last DOI dose.

assays.assay_description: 6-min forced swim test measuring immobility time as an index of passive coping/behavioral despair; tested 24 h after LPS (~48 h after DOI). Some cohorts had OFT 2 h prior; pooled with FST-only cohort after confirming no effect of prior OFT.

application_type.evidence: DOI (0.3 or 1.0 mg/kg) or vehicle was administered 24 h prior to LPS (1 mg/kg) or vehicle ... administered intraperitoneally (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were habituated to the testing room for 1 h before each assay (room acclimation only, no apparatus habituation).

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice swim freely in the cylinder; no head/body restraint applied.

food_restriction.evidence: No food accessible inside the swim cylinder during the 6-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water accessible; test medium is water but not drinkable.

time_to_assay.evidence: DOI ... administered 24 h prior to LPS ... behavioral testing was conducted 24 h later (~48 h after DOI).

sample_size.evidence: Mice (n = 16-21) were pretreated (i.p.) with DOI (0.3 or 1 mg/kg) or saline 24 h prior to LPS (1 mg/kg, i.p.), and immobility time in the FST was tested 24 h later.

outcomes.summary: LPS markedly increased FST immobility time relative to saline controls. DOI pretreatment significantly reduced LPS-induced immobility at both 0.3 and 1 mg/kg, with a stronger effect at the lower dose.
outcomes.evidence: LPS markedly increased immobility time relative to saline treatment ... DOI pretreatment significantly reduced LPS-induced immobility at both tested doses, with the effect more pronounced at the lower dose (0.3 mg/kg) compared with the higher dose (1 mg/kg).

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility is not an ethological behaviour (rubric example).

B6_cognitive.evidence: FST does not require learning or memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: No pose-estimation or ML-based behavioural classifier described.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or drinking water accessible during FST.

D1_continuity.evidence: Animals underwent the FST for 6 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: FST performed on a single day per cohort.

D5_followup.evidence: FST conducted ~48 h after DOI administration (≥24 h after last drug).

assays.assay_description: Daily body-weight measurement immediately before LPS and once daily for 7 days following LPS challenge to assess recovery from LPS-induced weight loss; data analysed as time course and AUC.

application_type.evidence: Mice were pretreated (i.p.) with DOI (0.3 or 1 mg/kg) or saline 24 h prior to LPS (1 mg/kg, i.p.).

setup_restrain.evidence: Brief weighing only; no restraint described during the measurement.

food_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum

time_to_assay.evidence: body weight was measured immediately before LPS injection and once daily for the following 7 days (first post-DOI measurement at 24 h, last at ~8 days post-DOI).

sample_size.evidence: Mice (n = 6-8) ... body weight was measured immediately before LPS injection and once daily for the following 7 days.

outcomes.summary: LPS produced a sharp drop in body weight within 24 h followed by slow recovery, significantly increasing 7-day AUC of weight change. DOI pretreatment at both 0.3 and 1 mg/kg significantly attenuated cumulative body-weight loss.
outcomes.evidence: LPS significantly increased the AUC relative to saline controls ... Pretreatment with DOI at both 0.3 and 1 mg/kg significantly attenuated this cumulative weight loss.

B4_ethological.evidence: Body weight is a physiological measure.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Mice were returned to their home cages; body weight measured in home-cage housing.

E3_bedding.evidence: Home cage with standard bedding (implied by group housing in cages).

E8_food_water.evidence: food and water provided ad libitum in home cage.

D1_continuity.evidence: body weight was measured immediately before LPS injection and once daily for the following 7 days.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Measured before LPS and daily for 7 days following (≥7 recording days).

D4_baseline.evidence: body weight was measured immediately before LPS injection

D5_followup.evidence: Daily measurements for 7 days post-LPS (and ≥24 h after DOI).

D6_circadian.evidence: Each weighing brief; no single session ≥6 h.

judge_notes: All candidates agreed on OFT and FST as separate assays; consolidated both with modal scoring.

Added Body Weight Monitoring as a third assay — candidates omitted it but the paper explicitly measures and analyzes daily body weight over 7 days as a behavioural/physiological readout following DOI+LPS, reported with statistics and group comparisons (Fig. 6D-E). Scored conservatively as home-cage measure.
B1 for OFT scored 1 (2-3 measures: total distance + center time); FST B1 scored 0 (immobility only).

OFT outcome direction: judged 'mixed' — LPS decreased locomotion, DOI 0.3 mg/kg restored to control, 1 mg/kg did not; primary directional framing ambiguous, but the paper's narrative is restoration (which could be 'increase' from LPS-depressed baseline). Selected 'mixed' to reflect divergent dose effects.
setup_habituation scored 'no' for OFT/FST since the paper describes only room acclimation (1 h), which per rubric does NOT count as apparatus habituation.
time_to_assay = short_term_1to7d (~48 h after last DOI dose) because behavioral testing is 24 h after LPS, which itself is 24 h after DOI.
DOI dose list consolidated to include all five tested doses (0.1, 0.3, 0.56, 1.0, 2.0 mg/kg) used in the dose-response study, even though only 0.3 and 1.0 were used prophylactically.
enrichment_housing kept as 'not_reported' — paper describes housing but does not mention enrichment items.
